hit Alt+F2, type in kpackagekit, and the program managing software will start. 
There search for rkward and install it - should be pretty much intuitive, so I 
will not write details here.

hope it helps,

Donatas

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

unfortunately, RKWard is badly broken in Ubuntu 9.04. Meik Michalke provides 
up-to-date working packages in a private repository, as detailed on 
http://sourceforge.net/apps/mediawiki/rkward/index.php?title=Binaries_and_Build_Scripts#Unofficial_Ubuntu_repositories 
. Running the following in a console window should do the trick:

   sudo echo "deb http://reaktanz.de/deb/rkward jaunty main" > 
/etc/apt/sources.list.d/rkward.list
   sudo apt-get update
   sudo apt-get install rkward

Regards
Thomas

Hi,

On Tuesday 04 August 2009, alexandre villers wrote:
> I just had a problem with the directory where RKward stores downloaded

> did not match /.rkward/package_archive).

I'm afraid I did not quite understand the problem. Could you give some more 
detail on what is (not) happening, and what you expect to happen?

Note that two directories really are involved. First, R downloads the package 
sources to some directory. This is ~/.rkward/package_archive by default, if 
Settings->Configure RKWard->R packages->Archive downloaded packages is checked. 
Else the source packages are downloaded to a temporary directory.
In a second step, the packages are installed in the R library directory.

Regards
Thomas

messages.subject: [rkward-users] [rkward - Help] RE: How to use Intervals package?
messages.subject_clean: [rkward-users] [rkward - Help] RE: How to use Intervals package?
messages.body_plain:
Read and respond to this message at: 
https://sourceforge.net/forum/message.php?msg_id=7559724
By: tfry

The short answer is, RKWard does not have any built-in support for this package
(i.e. no graphical menus/dialogs), so you will have to use the R Console ("Console
de R").

For a slightly longer answer: Unfortunately, there is not yet a standard way
to get information on a package. But after loading the package, you can switch
to the Workspace Browser (Espaco de trabajo), right click on any of the functions
in the package, and chose "Search Help". That has links to an index page, and
in the case of the interval package, the index has a link to an overview in
PDF format. Read that first, and see if it answers your questions.

If after that you feel completely lost, perhaps take a thorough look at this,
first: Help->Help on R->An Introduction to R.

If you feel you understand the basics, but just can't get this or that to work,
feel free to come back with a more specific question. However, in that case
you may want to post to r-help, instead, to profit from the larger user base
(see http://www.r-project.org/posting-guide.html).

If you get things to work, alright, but you think RKWard should really offer
a graphical user interface for that, consider contributing a plugin:
http://rkward.sourceforge.net/documents/devel/plugins/index.html

messages.subject: [rkward-users] Installation on Windows
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

the windows version of RKWard is still very young, and we have not gathered 
too much experience, so far. Therefore, sorry if the following is mostly a bit 
of guesswork, and no definite answer:

On Wednesday 26 August 2009, Fernando Saldanha wrote:
> I chose MinGW when installing KDE stable 4.3.0.  I noticed that the
> instructions for the KDE installation tell you to install
> kdelibs-mingw and kdebase-mingw. But these libraries do not seem to be
> in the list of the available libraries in the package selection
> screen.

I did not yet get around to try with KDE 4.3.0. If all else fails, you could 
try using KDE 4.2.3, instead, which is at least known to work (you may need to 
select the primary server "winkde.org" in the mirror-list).

The "-mingw" suffix is no longer shown in the latest version of the KDE 
installer, but as long as you chose MinGW-compiler initially, this should not 
be an issue. Just install "kdelibs" and "kdebase".

After KDE-installation, the missing library libktexteditor.dll should be 
located in [KDEDIRS]\bin\ . You may need to add [KDEDIRS]\bin and 
[KDEDIRS]\lib to your PATH, as described. (This is probably the first thing you 
should try, if you haven't done that, yet).

> On the PHP installation instructions I read "On the Components page,
> you need to select Program/CLI Executable." But I could not see any
> screen that would allow me to do that.

Looking at the screenshots at 
http://foundationphp.com/tutorials/php_installer.php (which is a generic guide 
for PHP-installation, NOT the sequence to follow to install RKWard), the title 
of the page is "Choose Items to Install" (step number 7). If your PHP 
installer looks completely different, please post some details on which 
installer you are using.

Regards
Thomas

messages.body_plain:
Read and respond to this message at: 
https://sourceforge.net/forum/message.php?msg_id=7598872
By: tfry

Could you give some more detail? Which version of RKWard is this, which version
of KDE libs, which version of R? Are you running in a KDE session or some other
environment?

What you are trying to do should really work (and should not even give any warnings
in R or RKWard). RKWard "captures" the R graphics windows, so this is the rkward
window that appears, but these should close automatically on graphics.off()
/ dev.off(). Some versions of RKWard did have bugs in this area, though. So
my guess is that you are using an old version of RKWard, and an update will
fix this for you (0.5.1 - for KDE 4 - and 0.4.9b - for KDE 3 - are current).

messages.subject: [rkward-users] Compatibility between RKWard and RGtk2
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I'm a new RKWard user and so far I've been quite pleased with the
environment it provides for R development. ?However, I'm wondering if
the compatibility with RGtk2 has been tested. ?The following simple
program crashes RKWard with a SIGABRT ::

    require(RGtk2)
    require(gWidgets)
    require(gWidgetsRGtk2)
    options("guiToolkit" = "RGtk2")
    gbutton("Hello world", container=gwindow())

(I would gladly use Qt widgets within R, but there does not appear to
be any suitable bindings available.)
I am running under Ubuntu 9.04 and RKWard 0.5.1. ?Here is the traceback I get ::
